items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: I had to accompany Al Moore, who was a trombone player, used to sing between sets. He'd go around with his trombone and sing. And he'd split tips with me.

ctx.x: I lived, I lived too far uptown for it. I didn't live in that, live in that section. Where were you living then? On Napoleon Avenue. On Jefferson Avenue. In the uptown Tulane section, the university section. But, uh. You went to Tulane, didn't you? Mm-hmm. Two years, until I found out that if I graduated I could get a job as a, as a brassman for fifteen dollars a week. So I said, I'm making sixty dollars a week playing music. I think I'm gonna stay with the music. No, I was, it was, this was just about in time…
Did you study music at all at Tulane while you were there?
